title: Input profiles gave no clear flicker prediction gain across nine held-out name groups in 32 fly visual types
abstract: We tested whether similar anatomical input profiles predict mean flicker response shape outside represented cell type name groups. We reused verified public summaries for 271 neurons from 57 flies in 32 types. Each outer fit held out the target name group and all imaging flies of the target type. Inner tuning used the same exclusions. The combined male and female input-distance model had mean squared shape error 0.848884; the training mean had error 0.847207. Thus the relative gain was -0.20 percent. A type-and-fly holdout retained a 7.27 percent gain. The within-group anatomical label test gave p = 0.220. The central 95 percent fly-refit sensitivity range for absolute gain was -0.0462 to 0.0317; it is not a population confidence interval. In a post hoc check, 1 of 199 random partitions with the same group sizes had gains at most the observed name-group gain. The specified model did not show clear transfer across these name groups. Uneven groups, few cells per type, fixed anatomy, calcium trial means, and reuse of one activity cohort limit inference. Original code, aggregate results, figures, input hashes, and external regeneration steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Nested prediction error under four exclusion scopes in 32 fly visual cell types. The combined input-distance model has no mean gain over its training mean when name groups and target imaging flies are held out.
Aggregate name-group gains, within-group label tests, imaging-fly refits and post hoc random groups. Positive gain means less prediction error. Resampling ranges are conditional sensitivity ranges.

citations.reason: Uses verified small source arrays, sample definitions and prediction method. Adds full name-group and target-fly holdout, complete refit sensitivity and a post hoc random-group control. New code; same activity cohort.
Different signed visual propagation benchmark; no data or code reused.
